title: Behavioral Plasticity in Advanced Technology Adoption: A Cognitive Dissonance Analysis
content: This study uses a novel approach to investigate cognitive dissonance, focusing on the discrepancy between consumer belief and action in response to innovative technological product designs that have emerged in recent years. The study was designed to measure participants’ behavioral plasticity as they were asked to evaluate the degree to which they are comfortable with various AI-based technologies. Participants were presented with paired statements, each reflecting opposing values in relation to different categories of technology, including autonomous vehicles, video game design, smart home technologies, and the use of AI in healthcare. A 'dissonance score' was calculated based on the absolute difference between these paired ratings, providing a quantitative measure of the internal conflict experienced by participants. Findings indicate that adolescents and males are more likely to experience cognitive dissonance, suggesting that these groups make more significant efforts to reconcile their beliefs and practices in the face of conflicting ideas. For adolescents, this may be linked to their thinking patterns as they are still developing, making it harder for them to reconcile new technology with existing standards. These results emphasize the importance of trust and transparency in technology systems. By focusing on making technology feel accessible and ethically based, companies can help reduce the mental health of some users. Furthermore, this study highlights the importance of developing tools that meet the standards of various groups and ensure an inclusive approach to innovation. Further research is needed to understand better how cultural, social, and educational factors influence cognitive dissonance in technology use. By delving deeper into these nuances, future research can help develop solutions that push the boundaries of innovation and make meaningful connections with the people who use them. Ultimately, this research sheds light on how companies can create technologies that feel less intimidating and accessible, thereby providing trust and consistency of action among a wide variety of users.
